comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Wired and green in the suite, not yet eyeballed. `Surface` gained the three libghostty calls (mouse position, left button, read selection), `SurfaceView` reports a drag to the surface and copies on ⌘C, and the Edit menu carries Copy beside Paste with both greying out when they would do nothing.

What no test here can say is whether a drag actually produces a highlighted range and whether ⌘C lands the right text on the clipboard - that needs a window. To check: `./dev --bundle` (the bundle does not rebuild with `./dev -b`), launch it, drag across some output, ⌘C, and paste somewhere.

The comment claiming a pane's selection lived in the daemon was wrong and is corrected. Worth knowing why this was never blocked on a_27CTgqqdv: that card is about reporting a click to the program in the pane, which needs the pane's mouse mode - and frame diffs consume mode changes before this surface sees one, so the surface believes mouse reporting is always off. That is exactly what makes a drag mean "select" here and never "click" over there.

Still open: whether double-click-to-word and triple-click-to-line come free from the surface, and keyboard selection.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
The wiring is now pinned rather than only compiled. `SurfaceView` drives a protocol the shell owns instead of a libghostty `Surface` directly, which moved the two decisions no test could reach into the layer the suite already covers: the AppKit-to-surface coordinate flip (unflipped, a drag selects its own mirror image), and copying nothing leaving the clipboard alone. Tests write to a pasteboard of their own.

Still needs the eyeball, and only for the half no test can reach: whether a drag paints a visible highlight, and whether the text that lands is the text under the pointer. `./dev --bundle`, launch it, drag, ⌘C, paste.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Paste works and copy does not, which for anything involving a terminal is an hourly need. Reading an error out of a pane and putting it somewhere means retyping it.

Two halves, and only one of them is the thing that is blocked upstream.

Making a selection. `SurfaceView.mouseDown` sends a focus request and returns; nothing reaches the libghostty surface, so there is currently no way to drag out a selection at all. This is *not* a_27CTgqqdv. That card is about mouse buttons and motion being reported to the program running in the pane, which needs herdr to expose the pane's modes and is genuinely stuck. A selection is the surface's own - it is made against the grid libghostty already painted, and no daemon has to agree to anything.

Reading it back. AppMenu.swift currently says a pane's selection lives in the daemon where Muster cannot yet reach it. That is wrong for the pinned libghostty: `ghostty_surface_has_selection` and `ghostty_surface_read_selection` are both in deps/ghostty/include/ghostty.h, and the header also carries clipboard read/write callbacks on the runtime config. Worth correcting the comment whichever way this lands.

So: an Edit menu item beside Paste, reading the focused surface's selection, and enough mouse handling for a drag to make one. Selection also wants a visible highlight, which libghostty draws itself once it knows a selection exists.

Open: whether keyboard selection is wanted too, and whether double-click-to-word and triple-click-to-line come for free from the surface or need wiring.
title: 📋 Copy what is selected in a pane
